summary: Shows example output of listing one collection installed in multiple paths, and using `-p` with colon-separated paths to search extra locations, which are prepended to the configured search paths.
questions: How do I list collections in a directory that isn't in my configured paths?
Can I pass multiple paths to ansible-galaxy collection list?
Why does the same collection show up twice with different versions?

answer_card.title: List collections from extra paths
answer_card.answer_md:
Use `-p` with one or more paths separated by `:`. They are added to the **beginning** of the configured collections search paths:

```bash
ansible-galaxy collection list -p '/opt/ansible/collections:/etc/ansible/collections'
```

If a collection is installed in several paths, `ansible-galaxy collection list <fqcn>` shows each instance with its own version (e.g. `fortinet.fortios 1.0.1` in `~/.ansible/collections` and `1.0.6` in `/usr/share/ansible/collections`).
